summary: All three runs read as credible sets of Ltd accounts for the trades described: the construction pair show materials, sub-contractors, wages and plant depreciation on turnover of £75k/£112.5k, VAT boxes are nil only in the genuinely unregistered scenario and fully populated in the registered one, and the IT consultancy shows consultancy-shaped costs, payroll with employer NI, and asset additions/disposal handled through the fixed asset note. Nothing blocks the runs; the concerns below are for a human to look at.

concerns.figure: Marginal relief warning: corporation tax £28,028.78 vs expected £36,880 on chargeable profit £147,519.90
concerns.where: ltd-scenario-full, Compliance Checks last row and Corporation Tax (CT600) section / CorporationTax!K35
concerns.why: The report's own check flags that with profits well over £50,000 the marginal/main-rate calculation is not being applied; the charge is computed at an effective rate below the expected figure. The report explains this as a warning, so it is not blocking, but the CT charge should be verified against the correct rate bands.

concerns.figure: Corporation tax for the year in the fixed asset note £28,028.78 against CT600 tax payable £13,995.22
concerns.where: ltd-scenario-full, Fixed Asset Note "Corporation tax for the year" (PubNotes D41) vs CT600 AJ126/AJ131
concerns.why: The published note carries roughly double the CT600 self-assessed figure (the same doubling appears in the VAT scenario: note £1,514.11 vs CT600 £756.02). One of the two presentations of the same year's tax charge is likely picking up both financial-year apportionment columns.

concerns.figure: Published Balance Sheet: Directors Loan £13,000 and Other Creditors £13,000, with net assets £195,053.12
concerns.where: ltd-scenario-full, Published Balance Sheet E29 and F31
concerns.why: The same £13,000 appears on two adjacent lines; if it is the same director's loan shown twice, only one deduction should feed net assets. Worth confirming the sheet is not double-labelling one balance.

concerns.figure: Published P&L profit before tax £177,279.90 against management P&L profit before tax £177,215.39
concerns.where: ltd-scenario-full, Published P&L F49 vs MnthP&L B45
concerns.why: The two statements report a different PBT for the same year (£64.51 apart, matching the tax-deducted-at-source figure in CorporationTax K37). Presentational, but the two profit figures should agree or the difference be explained.

concerns.figure: Bank and cash £250,544 against turnover £341,283 and opening cash £30,500
concerns.where: ltd-scenario-full, Published Balance Sheet E12 / Currentaccount.xlsx Sep A2 £238,864
concerns.why: Cash has grown roughly eightfold with no dividends and only a £7,000 reduction in the director's loan, so nearly all the year's profit is sitting in the current account. Internally consistent with the bank journal but an unusual pattern worth a glance at the bank workbook.

concerns.figure: Non-VAT construction scenario: chargeable profit -£9,046 and corporation tax £0 on an accounting profit of £1,754
concerns.why: The negative chargeable profit and nil tax follow from £12,000 of AIA on the year's plant purchase, and the scenario notes the CT600 profit boxes read nil by design, so this is not an error. Recorded only so a reader is not surprised by nil tax with a reported profit.
